correctness.rationale: Exact one-probe variance is 2(||A||_F^2-sum a_ii^2), and Cauchy--Schwarz bounds the diagonal-square sum by tr(A)^2/n. Real Schur--Horn attains this lower bound for every eigenvalue spectrum with a constant diagonal. Scaling spectrum to [1,kappa] reduces to maximizing Q/S^2. The single-coordinate derivative 2(ts-q)/(s+t)^3 has only a minimum internally; thus some optimizer uses endpoints. With r upper eigenvalues the objective derivative changes + to - exactly at r=n/(kappa+1), so neighboring integer multiplicities suffice, including kappa=1 zero case. Corrected no unsupported inference from finite grid: independent exact Fraction check n=2..35 with rational kappa plus n=4,kappa=3 witness 1/6; analytic proof covers continuum.
